scope: Proposition 16.3 (Prepared exterior with physical margin) of the manuscript “Spacetime Penrose inequalities: enclosing area, charge, and rigidity” (preprints/Spacetime-Penrose-inequalities-enclosing-area-charge-and-rigidity-October-5-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 794bf524061c4b36), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 105. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The thresholds and exterior above can be chosen with their stated full-region right continuity and collars, and with the following additional data. There are constants Cb ≥ 0, Cw ≤ 0 and a smooth compactly supported function C satisfying (16.6) Cw ≤ C ≤ Cb, C = Cb − kBs near each black face, C = Cw + kBs near each white face, where kB > 0 is constant on each individual collar. Set (16.7) b− = cb − Cb < 0, b+ = −cw − Cw > 0. There is a smooth positive weight ρ, equal to a positive constant times r−4 y on the end with differentiated symbol bounds, such that, for every real h ∈ [b−, b+] and every x ∈ X, (16.8) |(h + C) trg K| + |∇C|g + ρ ≤ 1 2M0(x). The thresholds, full regions, exterior, collars, offset, assigned heights, and weight are all fixed before any elliptic deformation parameter. After fixing the thresholds and collars, the offset can have arbitrarily small C1 norm. The constants of an absent face type remain valid bounds. Equation (16.4) holds.
